title: Device-independent Certification Of Majorana Fermions And A New Self-testing Equivalence
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 24 October 2026;
tldr: The paper introduces a device-independent certification scheme for Majorana fermions and establishes a new self-testing equivalence relevant to Bell-nonlocality-based verification.
motivation: Majorana fermions are central to topological quantum information but are difficult to certify under minimal assumptions; device-independent methods offer a strong route to verifying their quantum properties.
method: The authors develop a self-testing framework and derive a new equivalence relation that enables device-independent certification of Majorana fermion observables from Bell-type correlations.
result: They obtain a device-independent certification protocol for Majorana fermions and show a new self-testing equivalence that connects the relevant quantum correlations to the target Majorana physics.
conclusion: The work advances self-testing and device-independent certification in quantum information, with implications for verifying topological quantum systems under minimal device assumptions.

title: Efficient Multi-basis Quantum Position Verification Secure Against Generalized Adversaries
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 31 October 2026;
tldr: The paper proposes an efficient multi-basis quantum position verification protocol and proves its security against generalized adversaries.
motivation: Quantum position verification aims to certify a prover's spatial location using quantum communication, but practical schemes must remain secure against broad adversarial strategies while being efficient.
method: The authors develop a multi-basis quantum position verification scheme and provide a security analysis against generalized adversaries within a quantum cryptographic framework.
result: The protocol is claimed to achieve efficient multi-basis position verification with security guarantees against generalized adversarial attacks.
conclusion: This work advances quantum position verification by combining efficiency with stronger adversarial security, contributing to quantum cryptography security proofs.

title: Unifying Quantum Smoothing Theories With Extended Retrodiction
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 01 November 2026;
tldr: The paper proposes a unifying framework for quantum smoothing theories based on extended retrodiction.
motivation: Quantum smoothing and retrodiction formalisms have been developed in separate contexts, motivating a unified information-theoretic treatment.
method: The authors develop an extended retrodiction framework and use it to connect and compare existing quantum smoothing theories.
result: The framework clarifies relationships among quantum smoothing approaches and shows how they can be understood within a common retrodictive structure.
conclusion: This unification provides a cleaner conceptual and technical foundation for quantum smoothing and retrodiction in quantum information theory.

title: Experimental Characterization Of The Qubit-mediated Coupling Between Two Waveguides
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 29 October 2026;
tldr: An experimental study characterizing how a superconducting qubit mediates tunable coupling between two microwave waveguides.
motivation: Controllable coupling between propagating microwave modes via a nonlinear element is a key ingredient for microwave-domain quantum links, on-chip entanglement distribution, and tunable coupler architectures in circuit QED.
method: The authors fabricate a device in which a superconducting qubit couples two transmission-line waveguides and perform spectroscopic and scattering-parameter measurements to extract the effective qubit-mediated waveguide-waveguide coupling strength and its dependence on qubit parameters.
result: The measurements demonstrate that the qubit induces a well-characterized, tunable effective coupling between the two waveguides, in quantitative agreement with the circuit-QED model of the device.
conclusion: The work establishes qubit-mediated waveguide coupling as a calibrated, experimentally accessible resource for microwave quantum interconnects and tunable coupling in superconducting circuits.

title: Fault-tolerant Quantum Error Correction For Constant-excitation Stabilizer Codes Under Coherent Noise
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 02 November 2026;
tldr: This paper develops fault-tolerant quantum error correction methods for constant-excitation stabilizer codes subject to coherent noise.
motivation: Constant-excitation codes are useful for bosonic and photonic quantum information, but their fault-tolerant performance under coherent rather than stochastic noise is insufficiently understood.
method: The authors construct and analyze fault-tolerant error-correction procedures for constant-excitation stabilizer codes, using stabilizer-code techniques to handle coherent noise.
result: The work establishes fault-tolerance conditions or bounds for these codes under coherent noise and clarifies how coherent errors affect correction performance.
conclusion: The results support the use of constant-excitation stabilizer codes in fault-tolerant quantum information processing and highlight the importance of noise modeling in QEC design.

title: High-fidelity Flopping-mode Single-spin Operation Via Triple-dot Orbital-band Engineering
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 24 October 2026;
tldr: The paper demonstrates high-fidelity single-spin operations in a triple quantum dot using flopping-mode control enhanced by orbital-band engineering.
motivation: Spin qubits require high-fidelity coherent control, and flopping-mode electric-dipole spin resonance offers a promising route, but its performance can be limited by orbital and device-specific effects.
method: The authors use a triple-dot device with engineered orbital bands to implement flopping-mode single-spin operation and evaluate its coherent control performance.
result: They achieve high-fidelity single-spin operation, indicating that triple-dot orbital-band engineering improves flopping-mode spin control.
conclusion: Orbital-band engineering in triple quantum dots provides a viable path toward high-fidelity spin-qubit operations for scalable semiconductor quantum processors.

title: Scalable Neural Decoders For Practical Real-time Quantum Error Correction
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 28 October 2026;
tldr: The paper presents scalable neural-network decoders aimed at practical real-time quantum error correction.
motivation: Real-time decoding is a critical bottleneck for scalable fault-tolerant quantum computing, and neural decoders may offer fast, accurate alternatives to conventional decoders.
method: The authors develop neural decoder architectures designed for scalability and real-time operation in quantum error correction settings.
result: The work demonstrates neural decoders that can be scaled for practical real-time QEC, likely improving latency or resource requirements relative to existing approaches.
conclusion: Scalable neural decoders are a promising route toward practical real-time quantum error correction, though the contribution is more applied/engineering-focused than foundational quantum information theory.

title: Ultra-large-scale Compilation And Manipulation Of Quantum Circuits With Pandora
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 30 October 2026;
tldr: Pandora is a tool for compiling and manipulating ultra-large-scale quantum circuits.
motivation: As quantum circuits grow in size, scalable compilation and manipulation tools become necessary for practical quantum computing workflows.
method: The authors present Pandora, a software framework designed to compile and manipulate quantum circuits at ultra-large scale.
result: Pandora enables handling of very large quantum circuits, addressing scalability bottlenecks in circuit compilation and manipulation.
conclusion: The work provides an engineering/software contribution to quantum circuit compilation rather than an information-theoretic or thermodynamic result.
